description_en: The Umāmaheśvara or Haragaurī temple is located in a small square to the south of Mahāpāla Street en route from Mangalbazār to Mahāpāla. The temple square is surrounded by residential houses and has a small uncovered shrine of Śiva to its west. A vehicular road passes along the northern edge of the square.Thisśikhara-style temple stands on a three-plinthed base and columned porches. The triple-tiered plinth has aviṃśatikoṇa(20 corneredmaṇḍalaplan). The colonnaded top tier has 28 octagonal stone posts supporting the risingśikhara. Aside from the wooden door and metal pinnacle, the entire temple is made of stone. There is only one entrance of the temple, and it faces east. Two lions guard this entrance, and are situated in front of it on either side, attached to the first plinth. Behind them are two images of Nṛteśvaras, one for each lion. To the outer sides of the lions are twomoṭhas -again, one per lion. Five steps have been inserted in the plinth and lead to the entrance of the temple. Above the entrance is a stonetoraṇawith an image of Garuḍa in the middle. There are three more Garuḍa-toraṇasin the other three sides of the temple and at the same height of thistoraṇa.The main deity in the sanctum is Umāmaheśvara, and he stands on a stone pedestal. The temple has fourśikharaturrets in each corner, and four pavilions containing stone images of pair deities (Indra-Indrāṇī, Varuṇa-Varuṇī, Yama-Yamī, and Kubera-Bhadrā) on each side. At the four corners of this level, there are independently standing pavilions with intricately carved blind openings and triple tier moulded profiles as their roofs. The toweringśikharahas sevenrathas:the central plane has an architecturally framed opening on all sides, and terminates with a richly moulded cornice followed by a finial with a bell shaped bottom, a triple ring ofāmalakamotifs and a vase with a jewel on top. In the upper part of the temple, but still below the pinnacle, there are images of Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara facing in all four directions. In each of the four corners is an image of a lion with wings; each looks as though it is about to take off and fly. The fact that images of Lokeśvara have been placed on top of this Śaiva temple is rather curious.There is a stone inscription attached to the northern wall of the temple below the Garuḍa-toraṇaproviding information about its construction. The inscription informs that the temple was constructed by Vaṁśīdhara Bhāro in 1756. At the same time aguṭhīwas established donating lands for the daily and annual ritual worships. Nowadays, however, neither theguṭhīis preserved nor is the daily ritual worship observed.Towards the east of the temple, there is a small shrine with aśivaliṅgaknown asNhagaleśvara Mahādeva.
description_ne: मङ्गलबजारबाट महापाल जाने बाटोको दक्षिणपट्टि सानो चोकमा यो मन्दिर रहेको छ । मन्दिरको वरिपरि आवासीय घरहरू रहेका छन् भने यसको पश्चिमपट्टि न्हागलेश्वर भनिने सानो शिवमन्दिर रहेको छ ।शिखर शैलीको यो उमामहेश्वर मन्दिर विंशतिकोण मण्डल संरचनामा बनेको तीन तहको पेटीमाथि उभिएको छ । मन्दिरको शिखरसंरचना २८ वटा आठकुने शिलास्तम्भमाथि निर्मित छ । मन्दिरको माथिल्लो गारोको चारै कुनाका उपशिखरमा शक्ति सहितका चार  मूर्तिहरू राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरको उचो भागको चार कुनामा उड्दै  गरेका सिंहहरू  राखिएका छन् भने चारै दिशामा पद्मपाणि लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति खडा गरिएको छ । शैव मन्दिरको उचो भागमा बौद्ध मूर्तिको यो उपस्थितिलाई विशेष रूपमा हेर्न सकिन्छ ।मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा उमामहेश्वरको मूर्ति रहेको छ । मन्दिरको उत्तरी गाह्रोमा गरुड तोरणको मुनि रहेको शिलालेखमा मन्दिरको निर्माणसम्बन्धी जानकारी दिइएको छ । जस अनुसार सन् १७५६ मा वंशीधर भारोले यो मन्दिर बनाएर मन्दिरको दैनिक एवं अन्य पूजाआजाका लागि गुठी राख्न जग्गादान गरेका थिए । तर अहिले गुठी पनि सुरक्षित छैन र दैनिक पूजा पनि भएको देखिँदैन ।

historical_events.event_description: Renovation of the Umāmaheśvara Temple by the Ṭola Sevā Samiti
The temple was constructed by Vaṁsidhara Bhāro in the name of his elder brother Gauriśankara Bhāro.
Metal roof was fixed to the Nhāgaleśvara temple. Stone tiles were fixed on the floor of the shrine and small bell was hung up.

Kamalākānta Upādhyāye of Patan Svatha Ṭola made a request to the authorities (most probably to the Prime minister Candra Śamśera) to retain his priestly duties in this temple. Sahadatta Miśra from Patan's Mahāpāla Ṭola, and Kṛṣṇacandra Jhā from Cīkaṃmugala Ṭola also claim be the legitimate priest of the temple.
